en.title: Fewest Global Value Merges to Make Equal Values Contiguous
en.description:
One operation chooses two different values x and y and replaces every x in the array with y simultaneously. In the end, all occurrences of each value must lie in one contiguous block; find the minimum number of operations. You cannot change just one occurrence, nor delete elements.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the array. The original snapshot had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, −10^9≤element≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 0 and 2. The first example is not only about handling the repeated 1s; the 2 and 3 sandwiched between the two 1s must also be merged in the end.
hints: Record the last occurrence of each value and scan to get the maximum number of independent contiguous intervals; the answer is the original number of distinct values minus the number of independent intervals.
